question: Which complaint types with more than 3000 total requests from 2011 to 2020 show the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations with the daily average wind speed measured at station 744860 (JFK Airport), based on daily complaint proportions (the ratio of type-specific complaints to total daily complaints)? Please provide the complaint types and their correlation coefficients, rounded to four decimal places.
sql:
WITH daily_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) as complaint_date,
    COUNT(*) as total_complaints
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
  GROUP BY DATE(created_date)
),
daily_type_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(created_date) as complaint_date,
    complaint_type,
    COUNT(*) as type_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
  GROUP BY DATE(created_date), complaint_type
),
daily_proportions AS (
  SELECT 
    d.complaint_date,
    d.complaint_type,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(d.type_count, t.total_complaints) as proportion
  FROM daily_type_counts d
  JOIN daily_totals t ON d.complaint_date = t.complaint_date
),
wind_speed AS (
  SELECT 
    CAST(CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo, 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(da, 2, '0')) AS DATE) as weather_date,
    SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) as wdsp
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE stn = '744860' AND wban = '94789'
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2020'
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
    AND SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) != 999.9
),
combined AS (
  SELECT 
    dp.complaint_type,
    dp.proportion as x,
    w.wdsp as y
  FROM daily_proportions dp
  JOIN wind_speed w ON dp.complaint_date = w.weather_date
),
type_totals AS (
  SELECT complaint_type, COUNT(*) as total_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.311_service_requests`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_date) BETWEEN 2011 AND 2020
  GROUP BY complaint_type
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 3000
)
SELECT 
  c.complaint_type,
  ROUND(CORR(c.x, c.y), 4) as pearson_corr
FROM combined c
JOIN type_totals tt ON c.complaint_type = tt.complaint_type
GROUP BY c.complaint_type
HAVING c.complaint_type IN ('HEAT/HOT WATER', 'Outdoor Dining')
